sources.entry: chdb - In-process OLAP SQL engine with the full ClickHouse dialect, zero-copy pandas/Arrow interop, and federation to remote ClickHouse clusters via remoteSecure().

summary.one_liner: chDB is an in-process SQL OLAP engine built on ClickHouse, usable from Python (SQL, DB-API, pandas-style DataStore API) and other language bindings.
summary.what_it_does: chDB embeds the ClickHouse engine inside a host process so SQL queries run locally without installing a ClickHouse server. It can run one-shot queries via chdb.query(), or use connection objects with cursors and a DB-API 2.0 driver, plus stateful Sessions for multi-step pipelines. Input and output cover Parquet, CSV, JSON, Arrow, ORC and 60+ formats, and it can query pandas DataFrames and Arrow tables directly as Python table sources. The README also describes a pandas-compatible DataStore API that records lazy operations and compiles them to SQL, plus streaming results, Python UDFs, progress reporting, and AI-assisted SQL generation via configurable providers. Other bindings and a WebAssembly build (chDB-Wasm) are mentioned.
use_cases: run SQL on local Parquet or CSV files without a database server
embed an OLAP engine inside a Python application
query S3, MySQL or PostgreSQL data with SQL from Python
stream large query results in constant memory
build agent tools that let an LLM run read-only SQL
notable: In-process ClickHouse engine with no separate server to install
Pandas-compatible DataStore API that compiles lazy operations to SQL
Zero-copy style interop with pandas DataFrames and Arrow tables via Python(df) table functions
Stateful Sessions and DB-API 2.0 driver for multi-step SQL workflows
chDB-Wasm build that runs the engine in the browser
caveats: Python bindings are documented for macOS and Linux (x86_64 and ARM64) only
chdb-core allows only one active data path per process, so switching data paths requires closing first
Several language bindings are marked experimental, early, or unpublished in the capability matrix
